title: plugin-sharing: the record-share grant refuses a `group` recipient by naming sharing rules as its route, and the rule vocabulary has no `group`
body:
Filed by `domain:spec` seat 3 (seat post #18883, session `session_012uFegdfR6K6uqvLzt7XsdZ`). Source: the os-dev report `6153222151` on #23228 (PR #23324), an out-of-scope finding the dev did not fix in place. The seat re-read it on `main` at `404fc477e`.

## What happens

`ISharingService.grant` (`packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts:1345-1349`) refuses every `recipientType` other than `user` with one sentence:

> VALIDATION_FAILED: recipientType must be 'user' (received "group") — group/position recipients are delivered via sharing rules (ADR-0111 D7)

The sentence sends a `group` caller to sharing rules. But the sharing-rule vocabulary has no `group` recipient:
- `sys_sharing_rule`'s `recipient_type` select (`packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/objects/sys-sharing-rule.object.ts:172`) offers `user`, `team`, `business_unit`, `position`, `unit_and_subordinates` and `field`;
- `SharingRuleRecipientType` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts:460`) has no `group` either.

The nearest rule recipient is `team` (ADR-0090 D8: teams receive sharing). So the remedy the refusal names does not exist under that spelling. The dev's report cites a v17 rename for this; the seat could not confirm that citation and leaves it out.

Two smaller observations about the same sentence:
- A caller sending `unit_and_subordinates` gets the "group/position" wording, which does not name its value. The rules do carry `unit_and_subordinates`.
- The existing case `refuses non-user recipient types instead of persisting rows no gate reads` (`sharing-service.test.ts:1046`) pins the refusal, not the remedy it names.

## Why it is filed, not fixed in PR #23324

PR #23324 retires the `guest` value (ADR-0138 D8) and gives `guest` its own prescription. The right remedy for `group` is a choice rather than a mechanical edit:
- name `team` as the rule recipient a `group` caller should use;
- or say a record share's `group` has no rule route at all.

So it did not ride that PR.

## Ask

The generic refusal names a remedy that exists: for each non-`user` record-share value, the rule recipient that delivers it, or none. Pin the remedy text the way PR #23324 pins `guest`'s.
- ⛔ No change to which values `grant()` accepts. Only `user` is written (ADR-0078).
- ⛔ No change to the record-share vocabulary itself: `group`, `position` and `unit_and_subordinates` stay declared. ADR-0138 D8 rules only the guest keys.

Related: #23228 · PR #23324 · ADR-0078 · ADR-0111 D7 · ADR-0090 D8.
